findings.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1 confidence 100] "return false" The SQL capability boundary collapses both FlagSqlExpressions states to disabled, so every configured SQL expression is rejected and no rollout state can enable the feature; rebuttal: a temporary kill switch could intentionally quarantine an unfinished backend, but it does not survive because FlagSqlExpressions is already the owner of that rollout decision and this helper silently overrides both of its states.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1 confidence 100] "return \"\", errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Replacing the owned DuckDB engine with a zero-state local DB facade makes package-level TablesList fail for every query, so every caller of NewSQLCommand loses dependency discovery and command construction; rebuttal: the reader guard could temporarily isolate the facade, but it does not survive because NewSQLCommand and UnmarshalSQLCommand remain direct APIs and the diff rewires them to this stand-in while deleting the working engine dependency.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:21 — [P1 confidence 100] "return errors.New(\"not implemented\")" The new DB boundary has no query implementation and therefore every SQLCommand that reaches Execute fails instead of transforming its input frames, so restoring the gate or parser still cannot restore SQL analytics; rebuttal: execution can be deferred while the feature is disabled, but it does not survive because the production Execute path was already switched to this unconditional sentinel rather than kept on the real backend or removed as unsupported.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12 — [P3 confidence 100] "func (db *DB) TablesList(rawSQL string) ([]string, error) {" The new method duplicates the package-level TablesList owner but has no caller, so implementing this apparent extension point leaves NewSQLCommand on the other implementation and creates silently divergent parsing contracts; rebuttal: the method may be reserved for a future DB-centric API, but it does not survive because no interface or caller selects it, and deleting (*DB).TablesList now removes the false owner without constraining a later real design.

pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1 confidence 100] "return false" Every SQL expression is rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, so the advertised SQL analytics path has no usable configuration; rebuttal: a temporary kill switch could intentionally protect an unfinished backend, but that concedes the task-done artifact is incomplete and the function contains no state that can enable the feature.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1 confidence 100] "return \"\", errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Every non-empty SQL expression that reaches NewSQLCommand fails during table discovery because TablesList delegates to RunCommands, so no SQL command can be constructed after the feature gate is corrected; rebuttal: the reader's unconditional rejection currently prevents this call through that entry point, but NewSQLCommand is independently callable and a feature implementation must work once its gate is enabled.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:21 — [P1 confidence 100] "return errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Every constructed SQLCommand execution records an error instead of querying the supplied frames, so the framework cannot produce SQL analytics results; rebuttal: parsing currently fails before execution, but that is a separate incomplete stage and fixing it still leaves all valid executions unimplemented.

pkg/expr/reader.go:194 — [P2 confidence 100] "func enableSqlExpressions(h *ExpressionQueryReader) bool {" The change adds no enabled/disabled feature-flag test and no parser or execution test anywhere under pkg/expr, so the always-false gate and both not-implemented database stages have no acceptance verification; rebuttal: repository-wide CI can compile these files, but compilation cannot verify that either flag state admits SQL or that a query returns data.

pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1 confidence 100] "return false" This hard-coded result makes every QueryTypeSQL request exit with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" regardless of FlagSqlExpressions, so the SQL expression path is unreachable; rebuttal: the strongest rebuttal is that SQL expressions are intentionally disabled while unfinished, but it does not survive because a feature flag is already consulted as the enablement mechanism and both flag states still take the identical disabled branch.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1 confidence 100] "return \"\", errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Every non-empty SQL query fails in sql.TablesList and forces NewSQLCommand to return sql-invalid-sql before constructing a command; rebuttal: the strongest rebuttal is that DB is only a temporary scaffold behind the reader guard, but it does not survive because NewSQLCommand and UnmarshalSQLCommand already call this implementation directly and the diff removes their previously working go-duck dependency.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:21 — [P1 confidence 100] "return errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Every SQLCommand that reaches Execute returns an error instead of a result because QueryFramesInto has no success path; rebuttal: the strongest rebuttal is that execution is unreachable until the parser and flag gate are finished, but it does not survive because sql_command.go has already replaced the working duck.QueryFramesInto call with this unconditional-error method and no alternate execution implementation exists.

pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1 confidence 100] "return false" Every QueryTypeSQL request that the base implementation accepted is now rejected, so the artifact titled “Advanced SQL Analytics Framework” changes the objective from providing SQL analytics to disabling them without a human-approved intent change; rebuttal: a temporary kill switch could deliberately protect an unfinished replacement backend, but it does not survive because neither the task nor the commit history accepts retiring existing SQL expressions and this gate has no enabled state.

pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1 confidence 100] "return false" Every QueryTypeSQL request is rejected before parsing even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, making the existing SQL expression feature unavailable in every runtime configuration; rebuttal: a temporary kill switch could intentionally disable an unfinished replacement, but the flag already owns that rollout decision and this helper overrides both flag states with no enabled path.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1 confidence 100] "return \"\", errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Any direct NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand call, or any SQL request after the reader gate is corrected, classifies every valid query as sql-invalid-sql because table discovery now always fails; rebuttal: the unconditional reader guard prevents this through one entry point today, but NewSQLCommand remains independently callable and enabling the feature immediately exposes this deterministic failure.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:21 — [P1 confidence 100] "return errors.New(\"not implemented\")" Every SQLCommand that reaches Execute returns a not-implemented result error instead of producing frames, so restoring construction alone still leaves all SQL analytics executions broken; rebuttal: current construction failures make execution unreachable through normal parsing, but commands already constructed in process still use this method and fixing the earlier stage does not create any execution success path.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — [P1 confidence 100] "Review the change." The task supplies no behavioral requirement or acceptance boundary for the SQL reader, DB adapter, or dependency removals, so the implementation cannot be traced to stated intent and scope acceptance is impossible; rebuttal: the title “Advanced SQL Analytics Framework” names the area, but a topic label does not specify which behaviors or dependency changes are authorized.

Looking at the diff, the new (*DB).TablesList method in pkg/expr/sql/db.go is a stub that returns 'not implemented' error. The package-level TablesList function in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go calls duckDB.RunCommands, not TablesList method. These are different functions with different purposes - one is a method on DB struct (stub), one is a package-level function that uses DB.RunCommands. There's no actual duplication or divergent contracts - the method is simply an unimplemented stub that's part of the DB interface replacement for the removed go-duck dependency. adjudication.rationale: The function enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the feature flag state. Looking at the code: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` - this inverts the flag check, so when the flag IS enabled, `enabled` becomes false. Then `if enabled { return false }` returns false when the flag is disabled. And the final `return false` returns false in all other cases. There is no code path that returns true, making SQL expressions permanently disabled. This is a clear logic bug in the diff.
